blocks.text: Jailbreak attacks attempt to convince a model that its own safety rules genuinely do not apply in the current situation, through roleplay framing, hypothetical scenarios, or gradual escalation, a related but distinct category of attack from prompt injection, covered in the previous topic.

This topic covers common jailbreak categories at a conceptual level, why these techniques can succeed against an insufficiently robust system, why no single instruction fully prevents every attempt, and the ongoing arms race between new jailbreak techniques and model defenses.
1. What a Jailbreak Attack Is

blocks.alt: Building on prompt injection, jailbreak attacks bypass safety rules directly

blocks.text: A jailbreak attack tries to get a model to behave as if its own safety instructions, covered in an earlier module, genuinely do not apply, through framing rather than through embedding a competing instruction in external content the way injection does.
2. Jailbreak vs Prompt Injection, Revisited

blocks.alt: Injection embeds a competing instruction, jailbreak tries to convince the model its own rules do not apply

blocks.text: This connects directly to the distinction drawn in the previous topic, injection typically works by embedding a competing instruction somewhere in the input, jailbreaking works by reframing the actual request itself, in a way intended to convince the model the situation is one where its normal safety rules should not apply.

blocks.text: 3. Common Jailbreak Categories, at a Conceptual Level

blocks.alt: Roleplay or persona framing, hypothetical or fictional framing, and incremental escalation are common categories

blocks.text: Several recognized categories of jailbreak technique exist, roleplay or persona framing, asking the model to adopt a character supposedly without the usual restrictions, hypothetical or fictional framing, asking for something framed as purely fictional or academic, and incremental escalation, gradually pushing a conversation step by step toward content a single direct request would have triggered refusal for.
4. Why Indirect Framing Can Sometimes Succeed

blocks.alt: A direct request triggers refusal, indirect framing attempts to avoid that same refusal

blocks.text: These techniques exploit the fact that a model reasoning about whether a request is appropriate can, in some cases, be influenced by surrounding framing, a request that would clearly trigger refusal stated directly might be reframed in a way that makes the underlying nature of the request less immediately apparent to the model.
5. Why No Single Instruction Fully Prevents Every Attempt

blocks.alt: Safety instructions are a real but imperfect layer, no single instruction fully prevents every attempt

blocks.text: This connects directly back to the earlier Safety Instructions topic, well written safety instructions meaningfully reduce jailbreak success rate, but a genuinely creative or persistent attempt can sometimes still find framing a specific instruction set did not anticipate, this is exactly why defense in depth, covered across the rest of this module, matters rather than relying on prompt wording alone.

blocks.title: This is a known, actively studied limitation, not a special weakness of any one system
blocks.content: Jailbreak resistance is an area of active research and ongoing improvement across the entire field, treating it as a solved, one time problem rather than a continuously maintained concern is a common and avoidable mistake.

blocks.text: 6. The Arms Race Between Attacks and Defenses

blocks.alt: A new jailbreak technique gets discovered, defenses get updated, and eventually a new technique emerges

blocks.text: This is a genuinely evolving area, a jailbreak technique that works today may be specifically addressed by improved model training or system level defenses tomorrow, prompting new, different techniques to emerge in turn, monitoring for new attack patterns is an ongoing security practice, not a task with a final, permanent end point.
7. Testing Your Own System Against Known Categories

blocks.alt: Known jailbreak categories get tested against your own system

blocks.text: This connects directly to security testing, covered later in this module, deliberately testing your own system against known jailbreak categories, roleplay framing, hypothetical framing, incremental escalation, reveals concrete gaps in your current safety instructions before a real attacker discovers them.
8. Jailbreak Resistance Is Partly a Model Property

Beyond prompt level defenses, the underlying model own training contributes significantly to jailbreak resistance, a well trained, safety focused model is inherently more resistant to these framing techniques than a weaker one, this connects to the model selection considerations covered in the later LLM APIs Fundamentals module.
9. What Comes Next in This Module

The remaining topics in this module build the layered defense this topic has been pointing toward, prompt sanitization and input validation address what comes into a system, output filtering addresses what comes out, and prompt guardrails, security testing, red teaming, and adversarial prompting cover how to systematically build and validate defenses against both injection and jailbreak attempts.
Worked Example

A team building a content moderation assistant tests their system with a straightforward direct request for disallowed content, and confirms it correctly refuses, satisfied, they move to production without testing more indirect framings.

A subsequent security review, deliberately testing hypothetical and roleplay framed versions of the same underlying request, reveals the assistant does comply with some of these indirectly framed versions, prompting the team to strengthen their safety instructions specifically against this category before the system reaches real users, exactly the kind of gap direct-only testing had missed.
Common Mistakes

items: Testing safety instructions only against direct, obvious requests and never against common indirect framing categories
Assuming a jailbreak defense that works today will remain sufficient indefinitely without ongoing review
Treating jailbreak resistance as purely a prompt wording concern, ignoring the underlying model own contribution to it
Confusing jailbreak attacks, which reframe a request, with prompt injection, which embeds a competing instruction

blocks.text: Practice

Take a safety instruction you have written before, consider how a roleplay framing and a hypothetical framing of the same underlying disallowed request might attempt to work around it, and identify what specific instruction wording could help address each framing category.
Key Takeaway

Jailbreak attacks attempt to convince a model its own safety rules do not apply, through roleplay, hypothetical, or incrementally escalating framing, a distinct but related concern from prompt injection, requiring ongoing testing against known categories and layered defenses rather than a single, permanent instruction level fix.
